title: Don't Say Unnecessary Things
text: “Itsuki, after hearing all this, do you still think Naofumi is a criminal?”
“Bu-bu-buhi! Bu-bu-bu! Bu-bu-bu-bu-buh!”

The pig was squealing on and on. What in the world could it possibly be saying? When I asked Father about it later, apparently it had been shrieking about being kidnapped and demanding that its family and lover be returned.
“Naofumi-san! Even so, that doesn’t mean there’s no other crime here. I’ll ask my believers again—which side holds the truth, once more. Let’s judge after hearing both sides.”

At that, the armored knight glared at me with a furious expression before circling around behind Itsuki. It seemed they’d been kept from causing any further commotion. Judging that the situation had turned against him, Itsuki then left the scene without another word.
“Hmph… I should probably keep my use of this country as a base to a minimum.”
“Waah… Shadow Saint Hero, so cool…”
Kuro-chan, eyes sparkling, gazed at Ren—who’d just spat those words out about the country—with a look of pure anticipation. Seeing this, Ren looked troubled.
“Stop looking at me like that. Anyway, you can’t do your Class Up here, so give up on it.”
“Okaaay.”
“Good.”
“So then, is Kuro going with Shadow Saint Hero to the altar that awakens a new darkness—the Dark Sanctuary?”
“……No. Naofumi, keep this one properly restrained.”
“Yeah, yeah. Ren, thanks for getting mad on Kuro-chan’s behalf.”
“Ehh, but…”
“Hmph.”

With that, Ren left the scene. It didn’t seem like an atmosphere where we could manage a Class Up either. The Three Heroes Church folks were just squawking away as usual, and soldiers seemed to be gathering pointlessly all around.
“Buu……”
“…Let’s head back.”

Father was the one who brought it up. Fair enough—we’d already confirmed and registered the wave’s arrival time. More than anything, simply staying quiet about the differences in who we’d brought along and how the situation unfolded could change all sorts of things down the line.
“Indeed.”
“That turned into quite the commotion.”

“Well… yeah, I guess. Maybe I went a bit too wild within the country. Feels like I earned some needless grudges and missed my chance. Convincing Itsuki’s probably going to end in failure, going around in circles like this.”
“True. But it’s also something they brought on themselves. There were some familiar faces among the bandits.”
“…Slave hunters, maybe?”
“Yeah…”
“I see.”
The mixed-blood lizardman seemed to know something about the slave hunters.
“No need to worry about convincing Itsuki—there’s still a final option, I say! In another loop, Itsuki gave permission for it as a last resort.”
In the end, if we left it to Fleon-chan, it would all work out somehow.
“I’m intensely worried about what that even means, but fine, got it.”
“Honestly… it’s lamentable that thing calls itself a hero.”
At that, Father turned toward Rabbit Man with a full smile so cold it seemed to radiate black aura, practically sub-zero.
“Theo, you and I are going to have a little chat later, okay? Who was it that said something about being on the raped end?”
“Awawa… I—I didn’t say anything wrong!”
“Seems like your mouth runs just as fast making excuses as Itsuki’s does.”
“Hiiiiiyah!?”
And so, with Rabbit Man’s face turning pale, we set off for home.
“Motoyasu-sama, you saved us.”
“We did it. We pulled it off. Silence truly is bliss, I say.”

Indeed. If we hadn’t stopped Yuki-chan, we would have been the ones standing there instead. Rabbit Man, you went and lost control too—serves you right. Because of that, you’re getting scolded by Father for every last thing we merely thought.
“Shadow Saint Hero……”

Kuro-chan was positively brimming with curiosity about Ren. It was for the best that she’d taken such a liking to him. When we stepped outside the building, a Three Heroes Church pig was desperately calling out to Ren. It seemed to be pleading for him to come back and distribute the sand from the Dragon Hourglass, but Ren refused even that, ordering one of his companions to handle receiving it before walking off.
“Bow-wow!”
Wolf, who’d been waiting outside, ran up to Father, tail wagging away. Father gave a wry smile at the sight. Noticing that Rabbit Man’s face was pale, Wolf tilted his head.
“Kuun?”
“Ah, Theo went and said a bunch of unnecessary things inside the building, so he’s reflecting on it now.”
“Honestly… still, having him wander around so defenseless is worrying too. You feel the same, don’t you, Wolf? You want to protect him, right?”
“Kuun? Bow!”
At the mixed-blood lizardman’s words, Wolf tilted his head and barked as if nodding along.
“Yeah, yeah. Honestly… I can’t even tell who’s the master here anymore. Even if I can’t attack, I can at least run away, you know. There aren’t many people who could stop me right now anyway.”

Even without being able to attack, Father could still push, pin down, or grab things. He could probably even ignore an enemy’s attacks or grabs and just keep on walking, at this point. In that sense, it was reassuring. Still, there was the worry of Father getting surrounded and attacked by some strange group.
“Please be careful in that other country too. If anything, it might be even scarier over there.”
“True. Over there, more people follow instinct than reason, compared to humans. I definitely want you to keep someone nearby—someone who can serve as a weapon for the Shield Hero.”
“I’ll help, and so will Shion and Wolf. I suppose I’d be like a trusted blade, or maybe a rod?”
“Think of yourself as an axe.”
“Awoo~n!”
At the slaves’ words asking to be relied upon, Father let out another wry smile. Hmm… I couldn’t let myself lose out here either.

“Then shall I call myself Father’s spear? There’s the word ‘contradiction’—an unstoppable spear against an unbreakable shield—but an invincible spear and shield have no need to fight each other, I say.”
It left quite an impression on me, how Ark had drawn his shield the instant he gripped my spear.
“Thanks, everyone. You too, Motoyasu-kun. You’ve been a huge help. Yeah… well, I’ll do my best. Just, stop treating me like some frail maiden, okay?”
Father seemed bothered by it too.
“I wonder if we’ve drawn the Three Heroes Church’s attention.”
“There’s a possibility of that.”
Unfortunately, how far this influence would spread remained unknown, but I felt that Ren and Itsuki had at least been confronted with just how off this country was.
“We need to be even more careful than before… still, what struck me was that Ren’s actually kind to kids—he was pretty gentle with Kuro-chan.”
“He does seem good at looking after those younger than him, doesn’t he? Apparently he’s into raising up juniors.”
“Guess that’s a kind of playstyle too.”
“He said that in past loops, Father, you’d apparently been doing your own version of ‘junior-raising’ in a bad sense.”
“Well… judging by the way he gave instructions to his companions, it did seem that way.”

It was something only Father could really recognize. When Ren brought up that kind of talk after reconciling, in his later years he’d admitted to it. His reply had been something along the lines of, “I was immature back then too.”
“I just hope this doesn’t lead to any needless conflict or sacrifices…”

If there was one thing I absolutely wanted to prevent, it was any interference with the Filo-tan Experiment. Aside from that, we were acting differently than before. Even if the results turned out badly, I intended to protect Father, Filo-tan, and Filolial-sama through to the very end, no matter what.
“Whatever the case……”

Father was smiling at Rabbit Man with a grin that practically radiated killing intent. Sensing this, Rabbit Man’s face went pale, realizing there was no talking his way out of it now. Of course, during the meal after we got back, Father gave Rabbit Man a lecture. The content of the lecture was the same as the one Yuki-chan and I had received. Yuki-chan and I had learned our lesson well: even if you think it in your heart, don’t say unnecessary things out loud. Incidentally, the mixed-blood lizardman had also been made to stand by, partly as a target for the lecture as well.

Father wanted things like being pushed down to happen with mutual consent—but in Older Sister’s case, wasn’t he the one who got pushed down? There were parts of Father’s sensibilities I really couldn’t quite grasp. Did he push Rival down? No such thing ever happened. When it comes down to it, I suppose Panda might really be necessary after all.
Happy New Year! Thank you for your support this year as well.
